What prerequisites does it need in order to run on Windows?

@Martin Dvořák Thanks for the questions! For TorchLean CUDA training on Windows, you should mostly use WSL2 + NVIDIA driver + CUDA toolkit inside WSL. Native Windows CUDA is not wired cleanly here yet, but I will make this more clearly in the Readme and we are working on trying to support native windows as well: )!

9 messages were moved here from #Project announcements > TorchLean Codebase by Floris van Doorn.

We try to avoid any discussion inside any announcement threads, so I moved all messages after the announcement to this new thread (I thought this channel fits bets, but I can move it to a different channel if you think there is a better one).

Are there any long-term plans to support Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) or custom spline-based edge operations in TorchLean? Given the framework's verification and IBP setup, a formalized KAN would be incredibly cool for proving safety bounds and model interpretability.

Hey @Jinzheng Li ! That would actually be very cool and its on my list of networks to be added: )! The original authors of KAN are here at caltech so will speak more to them about this! If you want or know others, feel free to also open up a PR! Happy to discuss more: )!

very cool! Impressive that it binds straight to CUDA if I'm reading correctly - I kept looking for the libpython, then libtorch/libaten, but nope

shape safety is a big deal IMO - big time-waster and a barrier to abstractions, and requires dependent types with constant types to do correctly. It became a pet project for me in a few languages (Scala, Kotlin, then Lean), but only Lean has the full toolkit for types - my attempt was less ambitious than TorchLean though and just embeds a full Python runtime via libpython:

i see there's a Python export that generates string code, but if you ever wanted to make it importable from Python: it seems like a short walk to export Python bindings that directly construct an nn.Module via the Lean runtime; this would be pretty killer for integrating with existing ML projects

@Jinzheng Li Quick update: KAN support is now in TorchLean! We added a general KAN model with a pluggable KANEdgeFamily, together with a piecewise-linear triangular basis implemented using ordinary TorchLean operations. There is also a complete Auto MPG regression example. Full spline-specific IBP and end-to-end KAN verification are still the next step, but the model foundation is now there. I would love your thoughts or contributions!

@William Peterson Thanks! Since your comment, we have expanded the PyTorch bridge quite a bit. TorchLean can now exchange state_dict weights, capture supported torch.export/FX graphs into TorchLean IR, and emit PyTorch code from a TorchLean graph.

A directly importable Python package is still a great idea. I think the right design would be model-agnostic bindings around TorchLean’s graph and parameter representation, rather than bindings for individual models. Doing it properly is the hard part which I am figuring out as it means handling tensor ownership, autograd boundaries, packaging, and CPU/GPU memory without weakening the shape guarantees. It is definitely something I would like to pursue, but the current interop layer gives us a clean foundation for it! Will keep you updated: )!
That’s quick! I’ll pull it and play around with it for sure!
